state.case_summary:
A man in his 60s presented with a 1-year history of a pruritic, dark red plaque on his right upper eyelid. No remarkable medical history was noted.

A 4 × 2-cm erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with some papules on his right upper eyelid.

- Laboratory Tests: Routine blood tests and biochemistry analysis were within normal limits.- Histopathologic Examination:  - Revealed perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula  - Exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium  - Admixed plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells  - Alcian blue staining showed focal mild follicular mucin deposition- Immunohistochemical Analysis:  - Lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7  - Negative for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56  - CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1  - Monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated- Images:  Image A Title: Clinical presentation of right upper eyelid  Image A Description: 4 × 2-cm erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with papules    Image B Title: Lesional specimen  Image B Description: Histopathologic examination at original magnification ×50    Image C Title: High-power magnification of histopathologic examination  Image C Description: Shows atypical lymphocytes    Image D Title: Immunohistochemical staining  Image D Description: Shows lymphocytic infiltrates predominantly positive for CD4

root.label: Chronic Progressive Unilateral Periocular Plaque with Lymphocytic Infiltrates and Atypical Cells
supporting_facts: 1-year history of pruritic, dark red plaque on right upper eyelid
erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with papules
perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula
exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium
admixed plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells
excluded_candidates: Infectious etiology: lack of systemic symptoms and normal laboratory tests make this less likely
Autoimmune etiology: although possible, the presence of atypical lymphocytes and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement suggests a more specific diagnosis
salient_findings: pruritic, dark red plaque on right upper eyelid
erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with papules
